title: Hosted API headroom & peak projections — tokens/sec and QPS scenarios
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet projects Hosted API peak load (tokens/sec and QPS) across regions and maps those peaks to GPU fleet requirements and headroom targets for Q1–Q3 2026. It is a planning artifact for capacity purchases, reserved pool sizing and autoscaling configuration.

Summary of conclusions (TL;DR):
- Target steady-state utilization for reserved fleet: 60% (range 55–65%) to balance cost and latency predictability.
- Minimum global headroom to provision for sudden peaks (95th->99.9th transition): +40% on top of our 95th percentile expected load, satisfied via burst/PREEMPT pool and cross-region fallback.
- Region priority: us-west1 (primary), us-east1 (replica/high traffic), eu-west1 (growth). APAC should maintain small warm pool until demand justifies regional reserve.
- Immediate action: increase reserved A100 pool in us-west1 by 20 GPUs (A100-80GB equiv) to cover expected product launch spike in Mar 2026; enable autoscale burst to H100 pool in cloud partner for emergency +30% capacity.

Assumptions & definitions used throughout:
- Tokens/sec: user-facing token emission rate for generation endpoints. QPS: requests/sec for short-response endpoints. We map tokens/sec -> GPU usage by per-model throughput baselines.
- Latency target: P95 < 400ms for streaming endpoints at normal load; cold-start allowed in bursts with fallback.
- Models in catalog for mapping: "rw-large-7b" (optimized), "rw-70b-quant" (production quant), "rw-chat-16k" (chat variant).
- Representative request mix (Host API): 60% small generation (<128 tokens), 30% medium (128–512 tokens), 10% long (>512 tokens).
- Concurrent request batching window averages 8ms for short requests and 40ms for interactive; effective batching yields 1.6x throughput on avg.

Per-hardware throughput baselines (observed benchmark averages, conservative):
- A100-80GB: rw-large-7b -> 9,000 tokens/sec per GPU (mixed batch workloads). rw-70b-quant -> 2,100 tokens/sec per GPU.
- H100-80GB: rw-large-7b -> 14,000 tokens/sec per GPU. rw-70b-quant -> 3,400 tokens/sec per GPU.
- Small inference (distilled 2B variants) on A100 -> 22,000 tokens/sec per GPU.
Notes: baselines include small safety reduction (-10%) from lab numbers to reflect production variability.

Mapping tokens/sec to QPS (approx):
- Short-gen avg length 60 tokens -> ~tokens/sec_of_model / 60 => QPS-equivalent. Example: 9,000 t/s -> 150 QPS for rw-large-7b on A100.
- Medium-gen avg length 300 tokens -> 9,000 / 300 -> 30 QPS.

Traffic scenarios (global):
1) Baseline (current + organic growth): 95th percentile global tokens/sec = 38M t/s; 95th QPS (short+medium mix) ~110k QPS.
2) Launch spike (marketing + new feature): transient 99th percentile = 62M t/s; QPS ~170k.
3) Black-swan (outage fallback increases traffic to hosted endpoints): 99.9th = 88M t/s; QPS ~240k.

Regional breakdown (95th pt baseline) — projected for Q2 2026:
- us-west1: 46% of global traffic -> 17.5M t/s.
- us-east1: 30% -> 11.4M t/s.
- eu-west1: 18% -> 6.8M t/s.
- apac (shared apac pool): 6% -> 2.3M t/s.

Reserved capacity sizing (95th -> min GPUs to hit utilization target):
Calculation method: required_gpus = ceil( (regional_95th_tps * (1 + buffer_for_95th->steady)) / (per_gpu_baseline * target_utilization) ).
We set buffer_for_95th->steady = 0 (we plan for headroom separately). target_utilization = 0.60. Use conservative per-GPU baseline mix-weighted: rw-mix -> effective A100 baseline 7,500 t/s (weighted across models).
- us-west1: required_gpus = ceil(17,500,000 / (7,500 * 0.6)) = ceil(17,500,000 / 4,500) = 3,889 -> round up to 3,900 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved.
- us-east1: required_gpus = ceil(11,400,000 / 4,500) = 2,533 -> 2,550 GPUs reserved.
- eu-west1: ceil(6,800,000 / 4,500) = 1,512 -> 1,525 GPUs reserved.
- apac: ceil(2,300,000 / 4,500) = 512 -> 520 GPUs reserved (warm pool).
Notes: "A100-equivalent" meaning capacity may be mixed with H100; we translate H100 as 1.6x A100 baseline when planning purchases.

Headroom targets & burst strategy:
- Immediate headroom: maintain +40% burstable capacity above reserved pools (achieved via cloud partners, preemptible spot, and warm on-demand pool). This means us-west1 should have an additional ~1,560 A100-equivalent GPUs available via autoscale/burst.
- Emergency ceiling: ability to scale to +100% of reserved capacity within 15 minutes for region-level large events (via cross-region draining and partner hot-pools). Requires contractual burst with partner.

Projected fleet composition (recommended):
- Reserved (committed) pool: 85% A100-equivalent capacity for cost predictability.
- Flexible burst pool: 15% H100-capacity contracts and cloud partner on-demand for headroom.
- Reserve for heavy models (70B quant): keep a dedicated smaller pool of H100-equivalent GPUs equal to 12% of reserved capacity to avoid cold migrations.

Utilization policy & SLO alignment:
- Target average utilization: 60% for reserved pool. Plan alerting at 70% sustained for 5m to trigger expansion flows.
- Autoscale trigger: P95 latency > target OR sustained utilization > 72% (3m) -> add burst nodes.
- Scale-down: sustained utilization < 45% (15m) and stable traffic for 10m -> scale down up to 10% of burst pool every 10m.

Cost & procurement notes (high level):
- Committed A100 pools achieve ~35% lower unit cost versus on-demand. We recommend increasing committed pool in us-west1 and us-east1 before Q2 promotions.
- Negotiate burst SLAs with partner for 15 minute scale-up and guaranteed minimum availability for H100 pool during business hours.

Risk, mitigations & operational concerns:
- Risk: Single-region overload; mitigation: latency-aware smart routing to shift % of traffic to other regions and automatic fallback to smaller quantized model variants.
- Risk: Model latency regressions under high contention; mitigation: per-route quality monitors and automatic dynamic model-variant fallback (rw-70b-quant -> rw-large-7b-distilled).
- Risk: Spot/preemptible capacity preemption; mitigation: keep a 20% warm on-demand buffer and rapid checkpoint reassignments on runtime.

Action items (owners and timeline):
- Procure +20 A100-equivalent reserved GPUs in us-west1 (owner: Priya Desai) — target complete by 2026-03-15.
- Set up burst contract with CloudPartnerX for H100 pool (owner: Miguel Torres) — negotiate terms by 2026-02-28.
- Implement autoscale policy changes in runtime (owner: Jonah Kim) — PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/456, target 2026-02-20.
- Synthetic spike test (88M t/s black-swan) run and validation (owner: Eng-SRE) — test window 2026-03-01, ticket JIRA-INF-2187.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Approve 40% headroom policy vs. a more conservative 50% for peak-heavy quarter planning. Cost delta estimate required. (Finance + Eng leadership)
- Final regional traffic split for APAC (we have limited telemetry; product to confirm expected enterprise sales in APAC).

Appendix — worked example (us-west1 launch spike):
- 99th spike: 62M t/s -> with target util 60% and A100 baseline 7,500 t/s, required reserved = ceil(62,000,000 / (7,500*0.6)) = ceil(62,000,000 / 4,500) = 13,778 -> 13,800 GPUs.
- With existing reserved 3,900 GPUs, headroom required = (13,800 - 3,900) = 9,900 GPUs. We do NOT plan to reserve that many; instead we rely on burst partners and cross-region fallback (policy: allow up to 40% throughputs shift to us-east1 and eu-west1 under specified SLOs).

Notes to reviewers:
- Numbers above are intentionally conservative on per-GPU baseline to account for mixed request shapes and unknowns in production batching.
- If product plans change request-mix (more long-form outputs), re-run baseline mix and recompute required GPUs — long outputs dramatically reduce tokens/sec/GPU for the same QPS.

History of edits:
- 2025-11-08 A. Raman initial draft with baseline numbers.
- 2025-12-15 added region split and weightings after telemetry refresh.
- 2026-01-22 adjusted headroom to 40% after SRE review.
- 2026-02-12 updated procurement action items and PR links.

End of sheet — please comment inline with corrections, especially if you have more recent microbenchmarks for rw-70b-quant on A100/H100 or updated QPS telemetry.
